title: Cold-Chain Delivery Routing With Predicted Temperature Excursions
problem: Route planners for refrigerated delivery treat temperature as a fixed constraint and ignore how door openings, traffic delays and ambient heat change the load temperature along the route.
solution: A routing system models payload temperature with a thermal model of each vehicle compartment. For every candidate route it predicts the time-temperature profile using forecast ambient temperature, expected stop durations and traffic delay, then selects the route and stop order that keeps predicted excursions below a limit while minimising travel time.

elements.text: A thermal model of a refrigerated vehicle compartment that predicts payload temperature over time
Inputs to the model comprising forecast ambient temperature, expected stop duration and traffic delay
Prediction of a time-temperature profile for each of a plurality of candidate routes
Selection of a route and stop order that keeps the predicted temperature excursion below a limit
Minimisation of travel time subject to the excursion limit
Re-planning of remaining stops when a sensed compartment temperature deviates from the prediction

dependent_features: Door-open events are learned per driver
